title: Why Caesar Built a Wall Around His Own Army

scenes.headline: 2 WALLS
scenes.text: Julius Caesar surrounded his own army with a second wall.

scenes.headline: 52 BC
scenes.text: In fifty-two BC, Caesar trapped Vercingetorix and his Gallic army inside Alesia.

scenes.headline: INNER LINE
scenes.text: His first line of defences cut off their supplies.

scenes.headline: ≈15 KM
scenes.text: It stretched roughly fifteen kilometres around the hilltop.

scenes.headline: RELIEF ARMY
scenes.text: But another Gallic army was coming to break the siege.

scenes.headline: OUTER LINE ≈21 KM
scenes.text: So the Romans built an outer line, roughly twenty-one kilometres long, facing away from the town.

scenes.headline: BOTH SIDES
scenes.text: Now they had to defend themselves against attacks from both sides.

scenes.headline: DITCHES & TOWERS
scenes.text: Ditches, earthworks and wooden towers helped them hold their positions.

scenes.headline: SURRENDER
scenes.text: The relief army failed to break through, and Vercingetorix surrendered.

scenes.headline: TRAPPED & PROTECTED
scenes.text: Caesar's walls trapped one army and protected his own. Genius or desperation? Tell me below.
